post.caption:
Warm surface water flows north, cools, gets saltier and denser, sinks, and returns south along the seafloor. One lap takes around 1,000 years, and it is why London is far warmer than Newfoundland despite sitting further north. Melting ice dilutes the salt, which is the real mechanism behind those European cold snap headlines.
